Provides specialized enumeration for Allied Vision industrial cameras using the Vimba X SDK integration. This partial class handles discovery and management of Allied Vision machine vision cameras including GigE Vision, USB3 Vision, and Camera Link cameras. Integrates with Allied Vision's Vimba X library for native camera enumeration, device information retrieval, and GenTL provider management. Essential for professional machine vision and industrial imaging applications.
The namespace contains core components and utilities for VisioForge multimedia SDKs. This includes device enumeration, media processing, and various helper classes.
Provides comprehensive audio device enumeration capabilities across multiple platforms and APIs. This partial class handles discovery and monitoring of audio capture sources and output devices using GStreamer's device monitoring framework. Supports cross-platform audio device detection including DirectSound, WASAPI, PulseAudio, ALSA, and Core Audio with real-time device change notifications and permission handling for mobile platforms.
The namespace contains core components and utilities for VisioForge multimedia SDKs. This includes device enumeration, media processing, and various helper classes.
Provides specialized enumeration for Basler industrial cameras using the Pylon SDK integration. This partial class handles discovery and management of Basler machine vision cameras including GigE Vision, USB3 Vision, and Camera Link cameras. Integrates with Basler's Pylon library for native camera enumeration, device information retrieval, and camera capability detection. Essential for professional machine vision and industrial imaging applications.
The namespace contains core components and utilities for VisioForge multimedia SDKs. This includes device enumeration, media processing, and various helper classes.
Provides specialized enumeration for Blackmagic Design DeckLink professional video hardware. This partial class handles discovery and management of DeckLink capture and playback devices including video sources, audio sources, video sinks, and audio sinks. Manages professional broadcast hardware interfaces for high-quality video capture, playback, and signal monitoring with real-time device detection and signal loss notifications.
The namespace contains core components and utilities for VisioForge multimedia SDKs. This includes device enumeration, media processing, and various helper classes.
Provides GenICam (Generic Interface for Cameras) device enumeration for industrial and scientific cameras. This partial class handles discovery and management of GenICam-compliant cameras including machine vision cameras, scientific imaging devices, and industrial cameras using the GenICam standard. Supports camera enumeration with detailed device information, pixel format detection, and fallback mechanisms for robust camera discovery in professional imaging applications.
The namespace contains core components and utilities for VisioForge multimedia SDKs. This includes device enumeration, media processing, and various helper classes.
Cross-platform device enumerator that discovers and manages audio/video input devices, professional hardware, and network sources across all supported platforms. This class provides unified access to webcams, microphones, capture cards, IP cameras (ONVIF), NDI sources, Decklink devices, and industrial cameras (GenICam/GigE Vision). Supports both synchronous and asynchronous device discovery with platform-specific optimizations.
The namespace contains core components and utilities for VisioForge multimedia SDKs. This includes device enumeration, media processing, and various helper classes.
Provides Network Device Interface (NDI) source discovery and enumeration capabilities. This partial class handles detection of NDI video and audio sources over IP networks, enabling real-time video streaming and production workflows. Manages NDI device provider lifecycle, source discovery with retry logic, and maintains collections of available NDI sources for professional broadcast and streaming applications.
The namespace contains core components and utilities for VisioForge multimedia SDKs. This includes device enumeration, media processing, and various helper classes.
Provides ONVIF (Open Network Video Interface Forum) device discovery for IP-based security cameras and video surveillance systems. This partial class handles network-based discovery of ONVIF-compliant devices including IP cameras, NVRs, and video management systems using WS-Discovery protocol. Supports timeout configuration, cancellation tokens, and asynchronous discovery operations for professional surveillance and security applications.
The namespace contains core components and utilities for VisioForge multimedia SDKs. This includes device enumeration, media processing, and various helper classes.
Provides comprehensive video capture device enumeration and monitoring across multiple platforms. This partial class handles discovery of video capture sources including webcams, capture cards, and virtual devices using GStreamer's device monitoring framework. Supports platform-specific providers like DirectShow (Windows), AVFoundation (macOS/iOS), V4L2 (Linux), and UVC devices with real-time device change notifications and permission handling.

Cross-platform native library loading and mapping utilities for the VisioForge SDK. Provides automatic resolution of platform-specific native library names and handles dynamic loading of required native dependencies across Windows, Linux, and macOS platforms. This class ensures proper native library loading for ONVIF and other platform-specific components.
The DLL class handles: - Cross-platform native library name mapping (Windows DLL, Linux SO, macOS dylib) - Automatic architecture detection (x86, x64) for proper library selection - Runtime library resolution via NativeLibrary.SetDllImportResolver - Support for ONVIF camera integration libraries across all platforms - Fallback mechanisms for library loading failures This functionality is essential for proper operation of platform-specific features like ONVIF camera support.

Used by DSP Filters to Set the default Split Size. This is needed when a large Buffer arrives and the Application would't respond until the DSP is done. If the SampleSize of an Filter is Set to Value > 0 then the Buffer will be splitted at this amount of Samples and processed until all Samples are processed. After every Process, Application.ProcessMessages is called to make the Application respond to Windows. DefaultSampleSize is just a default Value. The SampleSize can be changed on every Filter seperate.

Static methods to convert between different sample formats.
Code is mainly based on information available on the original C source code pa_converters.c from Portable Audio I/O Library.
This class try to be as fast as possible without using unsafe code.
Dither isn't currently supported. Currently supported conversions are 'to' and 'from' conversions between the following value types:
Integer 8-bit (byte), Integer 16-bit (Int16), Integer 32-bit (Int32), Single precision 32-bit floating point (float).
Which are the most common PCM formats.
To use it, just call Convert. The compiler will automatically detect which method to call based on your data types. Couldn't be simplier.
int[] srcPcm16samples = new int[] { 1, 2, 3}; float[] destIeeeFloat32samples = new float[3];
SampleConverter.Convert(srcPcm16samples, destIeeeFloat32samples);
// destIeeeFloat32samples now contains the converted samples.

Advanced Audio Coding (AAC) audio in Audio Data Transport Stream (ADTS) format. The format block is a WAVEFORMATEX structure with wFormatTag equal to WAVE_FORMAT_MPEG_ADTS_AAC.
The WAVEFORMATEX structure specifies the core AAC-LC sample rate and number of channels, prior to applying spectral band replication (SBR) or parametric stereo (PS) tools, if present. No additional data is required after the WAVEFORMATEX structure.
http://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/dd317599%28VS.85%29.aspx

Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) implementation for audio frequency analysis and spectrum computation. Provides high-performance FFT calculations for real-time audio processing, frequency analysis, and spectrum visualization within the VisioForge SDK. Based on the Cooley-Tukey FFT algorithm with optimizations for power-of-two sample sizes commonly used in audio processing.
FFT capabilities include: - Forward and inverse FFT computation for complex number arrays - Power spectrum calculation for frequency domain analysis - Peak frequency detection for audio analysis applications - Optimized bit-reversal and butterfly operations for performance - Support for real and imaginary input data processing - Amplitude normalization for proper spectrum scaling This implementation is based on the 1998 version by Don Cross with enhancements for .NET integration. Licensed under a permissive license allowing commercial use and redistribution.
// Perform FFT on audio samples uint numSamples = 1024; // Must be power of 2 double[] realIn = new double[numSamples]; double[] realOut = new double[numSamples]; double[] imagOut = new double[numSamples];
// Fill realIn with audio samples... FFT.Compute(numSamples, realIn, null, realOut, imagOut, false);
// Calculate power spectrum double[] amplitude = new double[numSamples]; FFT.Norm(numSamples, realOut, imagOut, amplitude);

Integration guidance for GenTL devices:
1. Device Creation: - Requires a valid GenTL system handle from ArvGentlSystem - Interface ID and Device ID must be obtained from GenTL discovery
2. Device Operations: - GenTL devices inherit from ArvDevice base functionality - All standard device operations available through ArvDevice.cs - Camera-level operations available through ArvCamera.cs
3. Stream Creation: - Use ArvGentlStream for GenTL stream operations - Streams created through device's create_stream method
4. Error Handling: - Check for IntPtr.Zero return values - Use error parameter for detailed error information - GenTL errors follow standard GError pattern

Integration guidance for GenTL interfaces:
1. Interface Access: - Use GetInstance() to get the singleton GenTL interface - GenTL interface is automatically discovered by Aravis system - Available when GenTL producers are installed on the system
2. Device Discovery: - Use ArvInterface base methods for device enumeration - GenTL devices will be discovered through interface operations - Device IDs can be used with ArvGentlDevice.CreateDevice()
3. Interface Operations: - All standard interface operations available through ArvInterface.cs - GenTL-specific functionality integrated with base interface - Update device list and open device methods work with GenTL
4. System Integration: - GenTL interface works with ArvSystem enumeration - Appears in system interface list when available - Compatible with standard Aravis discovery patterns
5. Error Handling: - Check for IntPtr.Zero return values - GenTL errors follow standard GError pattern - Interface availability depends on GenTL producer installation
Example usage patterns for GenTL interfaces:
// Check GenTL availability if (ArvGentlInterface.IsAvailable()) { // Get GenTL interface IntPtr gentlInterface = ArvGentlInterface.GetInstance();
// Update device list ArvInterface.UpdateDeviceList(gentlInterface);
// Get device list IntPtr deviceList = ArvInterface.GetDeviceIds(gentlInterface);
// Open first device string deviceId = GetFirstDeviceId(deviceList); IntPtr device = ArvInterface.OpenDevice(gentlInterface, deviceId);
// Create camera from device IntPtr camera = ArvCamera.CreateCameraFromDevice(device);
// Use camera for imaging // ... standard camera operations ... }
Note: This is pseudocode - actual implementation depends on specific device enumeration and creation patterns.

GenTL (Generic Transport Layer) streams provide standardized streaming operations for GenTL-compatible cameras. This wrapper enables .NET applications to manage GenTL camera data streams with type safety.
GenTL streams extend the base ArvStream functionality with GenTL-specific features: - GenTL producer integration - Transport layer specific optimizations - GenTL buffer management - Producer-specific streaming capabilities

Integration guidance for GenTL streams:
1. Stream Creation: - GenTL streams are created through GenTL device instances - Use ArvDevice.arv_device_create_stream() on GenTL devices - Stream creation handled by GenTL producer automatically
2. Stream Operations: - All standard stream operations available through ArvStream.cs - Buffer management through ArvBuffer.cs - Acquisition control through ArvStream start/stop methods
3. GenTL Features: - GenTL-specific optimizations handled transparently - Producer-specific buffer management automatic - Transport layer optimizations integrated
4. Buffer Handling: - Standard buffer operations through ArvBuffer.cs - GenTL buffer allocation handled by producer - Memory management follows standard patterns
5. Error Handling: - GenTL streams follow standard GError pattern - Stream-specific errors reported through standard mechanisms - Producer errors integrated with Aravis error handling
6. Performance: - GenTL producers may provide optimized streaming - Zero-copy operations where supported by producer - Hardware-specific optimizations automatic
Example usage patterns for GenTL streams:
// Create GenTL device and stream IntPtr gentlDevice = ArvGentlDevice.CreateDevice(system, "interfaceId", "deviceId"); IntPtr gentlStream = ArvDevice.CreateStream(gentlDevice, callback, userData);
// Configure stream ArvStream.SetBufferSize(gentlStream, bufferSize); ArvStream.PushBuffer(gentlStream, buffer);
// Start acquisition ArvStream.StartAcquisition(gentlStream);
// Get frames IntPtr buffer = ArvStream.PopBuffer(gentlStream); if (buffer != IntPtr.Zero) { // Process frame data ProcessFrameData(buffer);
// Return buffer to stream ArvStream.PushBuffer(gentlStream, buffer); }
// Stop acquisition ArvStream.StopAcquisition(gentlStream);
Note: This is pseudocode - actual implementation follows standard Aravis streaming patterns with GenTL integration.
GenTL Producer integration notes:
1. Producer Discovery: - GenTL producers automatically discovered by Aravis - Multiple producers can coexist on the system - Producer selection handled by GenTL system
2. Stream Capabilities: - Producer-specific streaming features automatically available - Hardware acceleration where supported - Transport-specific optimizations integrated
3. Buffer Management: - Producer-optimized buffer allocation - Zero-copy operations where possible - Memory mapping for performance
4. Configuration: - Producer-specific parameters accessible through GenICam - Transport layer configuration through device interface - Streaming parameters through standard Aravis API
5. Compatibility: - Standard Aravis API maintained for compatibility - GenTL features accessible through existing interfaces - Transparent integration with Aravis ecosystem

Integration guidance for GenTL systems:
1. System Initialization: - GenTL systems are typically initialized through ArvSystem.cs - Use ArvSystem interface enumeration to discover GenTL interfaces - GenTL system instances are managed internally by Aravis
2. Interface Discovery: - Use ArvSystem.arv_system_get_interfaces() to enumerate interfaces - GenTL interfaces will be included in the interface list - Use ArvGentlInterface for GenTL-specific interface operations
3. Device Creation: - Use ArvGentlDevice.arv_gentl_device_new() to create devices - Requires GenTL system handle, interface ID, and device ID - Device IDs obtained through interface enumeration
4. Stream Operations: - Use ArvGentlStream for GenTL-specific streaming - Streams created through GenTL device instances - Standard streaming operations through ArvStream.cs
5. Error Handling: - GenTL systems follow standard GError error handling - Check return values and error parameters - Use GError marshaling for detailed error information
6. Memory Management: - GenTL systems are managed by Aravis internally - No explicit cleanup required for system handles - Device and stream handles require proper cleanup
Example usage patterns for GenTL systems:
// Basic GenTL system usage IntPtr system = ArvSystem.GetSystemInstance(); IntPtr interfaces = ArvSystem.GetInterfaces(system);
// Find GenTL interface IntPtr gentlInterface = FindGentlInterface(interfaces);
// Create GenTL device IntPtr gentlDevice = ArvGentlDevice.CreateDevice(system, "interfaceId", "deviceId");
// Create camera from GenTL device IntPtr camera = ArvCamera.CreateCameraFromDevice(gentlDevice);
// Use camera for imaging operations // ... standard camera operations ...

C# wrapper for Aravis USB Vision Stream functionality. This class provides type definitions for USB Vision stream operations. The USB Vision stream extends the base ArvStream functionality with USB-specific features.
USB Vision streams are created through the base stream functionality in ArvStream.cs. This wrapper provides type-safe access to USB Vision-specific stream features while maintaining compatibility with the base stream interface.
Usage: - Use ArvStream.cs for general stream operations - Use ArvUvDevice.cs for USB Vision device-specific functionality - This wrapper provides USB Vision stream type identification

Integration guidance for USB Vision streams:
1. Stream Creation: - Use ArvCamera.arv_camera_create_stream() for USB Vision cameras - Use ArvDevice stream creation methods from ArvUvDevice
2. Stream Operations: - All standard stream operations available through ArvStream.cs - USB-specific configuration through ArvUvDevice.cs
3. Buffer Management: - Standard buffer operations through ArvBuffer.cs - USB Vision payload handling automatic
4. USB Vision Features: - Configure USB mode through ArvUvDevice.arv_uv_device_set_usb_mode() - Set transfer size through ArvUvDevice.arv_uv_device_set_maximum_transfer_size() - USB bandwidth control through ArvCamera USB Vision API

Represents a GenICam-compliant camera device with high-level access to camera information, resolutions, pixel formats, and control features. This class provides a comprehensive wrapper around the Aravis library for industrial camera control.
Typical Usage Workflow:
Create camera instance using
Call to establish connection
Call to populate camera capabilities
Configure camera settings (exposure, gain, ROI, etc.)
Use for continuous capture or for single shots
Handle events for frame processing
Call and when done
Thread Safety: This class is not thread-safe. Access should be synchronized when used from multiple threads, particularly for streaming operations.
Resource Management: The class implements . Always dispose of camera instances when done, either explicitly or using 'using' statements. Alternatively, use for temporary disconnection without disposal.
Basic usage example:
using var camera = GenICamCameraManager.CreateCamera("MyCamera"); if (camera.Connect()) { camera.ReadInfo(); camera.SetExposureTime(10000); // 10ms camera.SetGain(0.0);
camera.FrameReceived += (s, e) => { Console.WriteLine($"Frame: {e.FrameData.Width}x{e.FrameData.Height}"); };
camera.StartStreaming(); Thread.Sleep(5000); // Stream for 5 seconds camera.StopStreaming(); }
API Update Notes: - Fixed acquisition startup sequence: camera acquisition handles device-level streaming automatically - Removed redundant arv_stream_start_acquisition calls that could conflict with camera acquisition - Updated buffer management to use modern Aravis buffer management APIs - Enhanced stream diagnostics with FillingBuffers parameter support - Improved error handling and logging throughout streaming operations - Added pre-flight checks for camera and stream handles before starting acquisition

Event fired when a new frame is received during streaming operations.
This event is raised from a background timer thread, so UI updates should be marshaled to the appropriate thread.
Frame processing should be kept minimal to avoid blocking the acquisition pipeline.
The frame data is copied, so it's safe to access after the event handler returns.
camera.FrameReceived += (sender, e) => { var frame = e.FrameData; Console.WriteLine($"Frame: {frame.Width}x{frame.Height}, Format: {frame.PixelFormat}"); // Process frame data... };
Event fired when a frame acquisition error occurs during streaming.
Common causes include:
Buffer underrun (camera producing frames faster than they can be processed)
Network packet loss (GigE cameras)
USB bandwidth limitations (USB3 cameras)
Insufficient system resources
The streaming will typically continue after an error, but consider reducing frame rate or increasing buffer count.
Event fired when streaming starts successfully.
This event indicates that the camera acquisition has started and buffers are available for frame capture.
Event fired when streaming stops.
This event is fired both for normal stop operations and when streaming stops due to errors.

Gets the current region of interest (ROI)
ROI as x, y, width, height
Sets the region of interest (ROI) for image acquisition.
X offset in pixels from the left edge of the sensor (must be within ) Y offset in pixels from the top edge of the sensor (must be within ) Width in pixels (must be within and x + width ≤ sensor width) Height in pixels (must be within and y + height ≤ sensor height) Thrown if the camera instance has been disposed. Thrown if the ROI parameters are invalid or the camera rejects the settings.
The ROI must satisfy the following constraints:
x, y, width, height must be positive
x + width must not exceed the sensor width
y + height must not exceed the sensor height
Values must respect the camera's increment requirements
Performance Impact: Smaller ROIs typically allow higher frame rates due to reduced data transfer.
Note: Some cameras may adjust the ROI to the nearest valid values based on their constraints.
// Set ROI to center 640x480 region camera.ReadInfo(); int centerX = (camera.SensorSize.Width - 640) / 2; int centerY = (camera.SensorSize.Height - 480) / 2; camera.SetRegion(centerX, centerY, 640, 480);
// Verify the actual ROI set var actualROI = camera.GetRegion(); Console.WriteLine($"Actual ROI: {actualROI.X}, {actualROI.Y}, {actualROI.Width}x{actualROI.Height}");

Sets the exposure time in microseconds.
Exposure time in microseconds (must be within ) Thrown if the camera instance has been disposed. Thrown if the exposure time is invalid or the camera rejects the setting.
The exposure time controls how long the sensor is exposed to light for each frame. Longer exposure times result in brighter images but may cause motion blur.
Valid Range: Use to determine the valid range for your camera.
Units: Microseconds (µs). Common values:
100 µs (0.1 ms) - Very fast, for high-speed imaging
1,000 µs (1 ms) - Fast, typical for motion capture
10,000 µs (10 ms) - Medium, general purpose
100,000 µs (100 ms) - Long, for low-light conditions
Frame Rate Impact: Longer exposure times may limit the maximum achievable frame rate.
// Set exposure to 10 milliseconds camera.SetExposureTime(10000);
// Set exposure within valid bounds camera.ReadInfo(); double minExposure = camera.ExposureTimeBounds.Min; double maxExposure = camera.ExposureTimeBounds.Max; double targetExposure = Math.Min(maxExposure, Math.Max(minExposure, 5000)); camera.SetExposureTime(targetExposure);

Gets comprehensive diagnostic information about the current streaming state and performance.
Diagnostic information including buffer counts, statistics, and error states. Thrown if the camera instance has been disposed.
This method provides detailed information about the streaming subsystem:
Buffer Information: Input, output, and filling buffer counts
Statistics: Completed frames, failed frames, and underrun counts
State Information: Whether streaming is active and stream handle validity
Error Information: Any error messages from the streaming subsystem
Troubleshooting Guide:
High Failed Buffers: Indicates camera producing frames faster than processing - reduce frame rate or increase buffer count
High Underruns: Suggests insufficient buffers or slow processing - increase buffer count or optimize frame handling
Zero Completed Buffers: Camera may not be producing frames - check exposure settings and triggers
No Input Buffers: Stream buffer creation failed - check memory availability
Performance Note: This method queries the stream in real-time, so it reflects current state.
// Monitor streaming performance var diagnostics = camera.GetStreamDiagnostics();
Console.WriteLine($"Streaming Active: {diagnostics.IsStreaming}"); Console.WriteLine($"Completed Frames: {diagnostics.CompletedBuffers}"); Console.WriteLine($"Failed Frames: {diagnostics.FailedBuffers}"); Console.WriteLine($"Underruns: {diagnostics.UnderrunBuffers}"); Console.WriteLine($"Buffer Counts - Input: {diagnostics.InputBuffers}, Output: {diagnostics.OutputBuffers}");
// Check for problems if (diagnostics.FailedBuffers > diagnostics.CompletedBuffers * 0.1) { Console.WriteLine("Warning: High frame failure rate detected"); }
if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(diagnostics.ErrorMessage)) { Console.WriteLine($"Stream Error: {diagnostics.ErrorMessage}"); }

Stops any active streaming operations
Cleans up existing camera and stream resources
Resets the disposed state to allow normal operation
Recreates the camera connection using original parameters
Usage Scenarios:
Camera was disconnected due to network issues (GigE cameras)
USB camera was unplugged and reconnected
Camera was manually disconnected using
Camera object was disposed but you want to reuse it
Recovery from communication errors
Important: After successful reinitialization, you should call to refresh camera capabilities, as they may have changed.
Alternative: For temporary disconnections without disposal, consider using followed by instead.
// Handle camera disconnection and recovery try { camera.StartStreaming(); } catch (AravisException ex) { Console.WriteLine($"Camera error: {ex.Message}");
// Attempt to reinitialize if (camera.ReinitializeCamera()) { Console.WriteLine("Camera reinitialized successfully"); camera.ReadInfo(); // Refresh capabilities camera.StartStreaming(); // Resume streaming } else { Console.WriteLine("Failed to reinitialize camera"); } }

True if streaming started successfully, false otherwise. Thrown if the camera instance has been disposed. Thrown if streaming cannot be started due to camera or configuration issues.
This method performs the following operations:
Ensures camera is connected (connects if necessary)
Creates stream and buffers if they don't exist
Sets acquisition mode to continuous
Starts camera acquisition
Begins frame polling timer
Fires event on success
Event Handling: Subscribe to before calling this method to receive frame data. Frames are delivered asynchronously via events.
Buffer Management: Buffers are created and managed automatically. The default buffer count is 10, which should be sufficient for most applications.
Thread Safety: This method is not thread-safe with respect to other camera operations.
// Set up frame handling camera.FrameReceived += (sender, e) => { var frame = e.FrameData; Console.WriteLine($"Received frame: {frame.Width}x{frame.Height}"); // Process frame data... };
camera.FrameError += (sender, e) => { Console.WriteLine($"Frame error: {e.ErrorMessage}"); };
// Start streaming if (camera.StartStreaming()) { Console.WriteLine("Streaming started successfully"); // Let it stream for a while... Thread.Sleep(5000); camera.StopStreaming(); }

// Capture a single frame with default timeout var frameData = camera.CaptureFrame(); if (frameData != null) { Console.WriteLine($"Captured frame: {frameData.Width}x{frameData.Height}"); Console.WriteLine($"Pixel format: {frameData.PixelFormat}"); Console.WriteLine($"Data size: {frameData.Size} bytes");
// Process the frame data ProcessImageData(frameData.Data); } else { Console.WriteLine("Frame capture failed or timed out"); }

Static class for centralized camera management and enumeration of GenICam-compatible cameras.
This class provides centralized management and enumeration of GenICamCamera instances to ensure: - Each camera is created only once and reused across the application - Simple open/closed state tracking with thread-safe operations - Thread-safe access to camera instances using concurrent collections - Automatic cleanup when cameras are no longer needed or available - Comprehensive device enumeration and discovery with real-time updates - Proper resource management and disposal patterns
Thread Safety: This class is fully thread-safe and can be used from multiple threads simultaneously.
Usage Pattern:
Call to populate the camera dictionary with available devices
Use to get a camera reference by device ID
Call before using the camera for operations
Perform camera operations (streaming, configuration, etc.)
Call when done with the camera
Resource Management:
Cameras are automatically cleaned up when they become unavailable. The manager tracks device availability and removes cameras that are no longer present in the system during calls.
// Enumerate and populate camera dictionary GenICamCameraManager.UpdateDeviceList();
// Get camera reference var camera = GenICamCameraManager.GetCamera("MyCamera"); if (camera == null) { Console.WriteLine("Camera not found"); return; }
// Open camera for use if (GenICamCameraManager.OpenCamera("MyCamera")) { try { // Use camera for operations camera.StartStreaming();
// Perform image capture operations // ... do work ...
camera.StopStreaming(); } finally { // Always close camera when done GenICamCameraManager.CloseCamera("MyCamera"); } } else { Console.WriteLine("Failed to open camera"); }
Thread-safe dictionary storing camera instances by device ID
Lock object for synchronizing camera operations
Base context for logging operations
Sets the BaseContext for logging operations throughout the camera manager.
BaseContext instance for logging. If null, a new default context will be created.
This method should be called early in the application lifecycle to ensure proper logging throughout camera operations.
var context = new BaseContext(); GenICamCameraManager.SetContext(context);
Updates the device list by scanning for available GenICam-compatible cameras. Automatically cleans up cameras that are no longer available in the system.
This method performs the following operations:
Calls the underlying Aravis system to refresh the device list
Compares current devices with cached camera instances
Removes cameras that are no longer available (if not connected)
Adds new cameras to the internal dictionary
Thread Safety: This method is thread-safe and can be called from multiple threads.
Performance: This method may take some time to complete as it performs hardware enumeration. Consider calling it on a background thread in UI applications.
// Refresh the list of available cameras GenICamCameraManager.UpdateDeviceList();
// Get count of available devices uint deviceCount = GenICamCameraManager.GetDeviceCount(); Console.WriteLine($"Found {deviceCount} cameras");
Populates the camera dictionary with discovered cameras without connecting to them.
This is an internal method that creates GenICamCamera instances for each discovered device and adds them to the internal cache. The cameras are not connected at this stage.
Gets the number of currently available GenICam-compatible devices.
The number of available cameras detected by the system.
This method returns the count from the most recent device enumeration. Call to refresh the device list before calling this method if you need the most up-to-date count.
GenICamCameraManager.UpdateDeviceList(); uint count = GenICamCameraManager.GetDeviceCount(); Console.WriteLine($"Available cameras: {count}");
Gets device IDs for all currently available GenICam-compatible cameras.
An array of device ID strings. Each string uniquely identifies a camera device.
This method automatically calls to ensure the most current device list.
Device IDs are typically in the format "Vendor_Model_SerialNumber" but the exact format depends on the camera manufacturer.
The returned array will contain "Unknown" for devices where the ID cannot be determined.
string[] deviceIds = GenICamCameraManager.GetDeviceIds(); foreach (string deviceId in deviceIds) { Console.WriteLine($"Found camera: {deviceId}"); }
Gets the device ID for a specific camera by its enumeration index.
The zero-based index of the device in the enumeration list. The device ID string for the specified camera, or "Unknown" if the ID cannot be determined.
Thrown when the specified index is greater than or equal to the number of available devices.
This method automatically calls to ensure the most current device list.
Device indices are assigned in the order devices are discovered and may change between enumerations.
try { string firstDeviceId = GenICamCameraManager.GetDeviceId(0); Console.WriteLine($"First camera ID: {firstDeviceId}"); } catch (ArgumentOutOfRangeException) { Console.WriteLine("No cameras available"); }
Gets a camera instance by device ID, creating it if necessary but not connecting to it.
The unique device ID of the camera to retrieve.
A instance for the specified device, or null if the device ID is invalid or the camera cannot be created.
This method returns a camera instance from the internal cache. If the camera doesn't exist in the cache, it will attempt to create a new instance. The camera is not automatically connected.
Important: You must call before using this method to ensure the device is available in the enumerated list.
Use to connect to the camera before performing operations.
// First, update the device list GenICamCameraManager.UpdateDeviceList();
// Get a camera instance var camera = GenICamCameraManager.GetCamera("MyCamera_12345"); if (camera != null) { Console.WriteLine($"Camera retrieved: {camera.DeviceId}"); } else { Console.WriteLine("Camera not found or could not be created"); }
Internal method to get or create camera instances with proper recreation logic. Handles camera reinitialization when needed.
The unique device ID of the camera to retrieve. A instance or null if the camera cannot be created or retrieved.
Thrown when the device ID is not found in the enumerated devices list.
This method handles the complex logic of camera lifecycle management including: - Checking if the camera exists in the enumerated device list - Attempting to reinitialize disposed cameras - Creating new camera instances when needed - Proper error handling and logging
Gets a camera instance by its enumeration index.
The zero-based index of the camera in the device enumeration. A instance for the camera at the specified index.
Thrown when the specified index is greater than or equal to the number of available devices.
Thrown when the camera cannot be retrieved or created for the specified index.
This method is a convenience wrapper that gets the device ID for the specified index and then retrieves the corresponding camera instance.
Note: Device indices may change between enumerations. For consistent access, consider using device IDs instead of indices.
try { var firstCamera = GenICamCameraManager.GetCamera(0); Console.WriteLine($"First camera: {firstCamera.DeviceId}"); } catch (ArgumentOutOfRangeException) { Console.WriteLine("No cameras available"); } catch (AravisException ex) { Console.WriteLine($"Error getting camera: {ex.Message}"); }
Gets all available cameras as instances from the centralized cache.
A list of instances for all available cameras. Cameras that cannot be retrieved are excluded from the list.
This method retrieves camera instances for all devices found in the most recent enumeration. Cameras that cannot be created or retrieved are skipped with a warning logged.
The returned cameras are not automatically connected. Use to connect to individual cameras before use.
Performance: This method may take some time if there are many cameras or if some cameras are slow to respond during instantiation.
// Get all available cameras var cameras = GenICamCameraManager.GetCameras(); Console.WriteLine($"Found {cameras.Count} cameras:");
foreach (var camera in cameras) { Console.WriteLine($" - {camera.DeviceId}"); }
Gets the first available camera from the centralized cache.
A instance for the first available camera.
Thrown when no cameras are available or the first camera cannot be retrieved.
This is a convenience method for applications that only need to work with a single camera or want to use the first available camera by default.
This method automatically calls to ensure current device information.
The returned camera is not automatically connected. Use to connect to the camera before use.
try { var camera = GenICamCameraManager.GetFirstAvailableCamera(); Console.WriteLine($"Using camera: {camera.DeviceId}");
// Open and use the camera if (GenICamCameraManager.OpenCamera(camera.DeviceId)) { // Use camera... GenICamCameraManager.CloseCamera(camera.DeviceId); } } catch (AravisException ex) { Console.WriteLine($"No cameras available: {ex.Message}"); }
Opens a camera for use by establishing a connection to the hardware.
The unique device ID of the camera to open.
true if the camera was successfully opened and is ready for use; false if the camera could not be opened.
This method performs the following operations:
Validates the device ID and retrieves the camera instance
Checks if the camera is already connected (returns true if so)
Establishes a hardware connection to the camera
Reads camera information to populate detailed properties
Thread Safety: This method is thread-safe and uses internal locking.
Resource Management: Always call when done with the camera to properly release resources.
Error Handling: Detailed error information is logged. Check logs for specific failure reasons.
string deviceId = "MyCamera_12345";
if (GenICamCameraManager.OpenCamera(deviceId)) { try { var camera = GenICamCameraManager.GetCamera(deviceId); // Use camera for operations camera.StartStreaming(); // ... perform operations ... camera.StopStreaming(); } finally { GenICamCameraManager.CloseCamera(deviceId); } } else { Console.WriteLine("Failed to open camera"); }
Closes a camera and disconnects it from the hardware without removing it from the cache.
The unique device ID of the camera to close.
true if the camera was successfully closed or was already closed; false if an error occurred during the closing process.
This method performs the following operations:
Stops any active streaming on the camera
Disconnects the camera from the hardware
Keeps the camera instance in cache for potential reuse
Thread Safety: This method is thread-safe and uses internal locking.
Resource Management: This method properly releases hardware resources while maintaining the camera instance for future use.
Idempotent: It's safe to call this method multiple times on the same camera.
string deviceId = "MyCamera_12345";
// Open camera if (GenICamCameraManager.OpenCamera(deviceId)) { try { // Use camera... var camera = GenICamCameraManager.GetCamera(deviceId); camera.StartStreaming(); // ... perform operations ... } finally { // Always close when done bool closed = GenICamCameraManager.CloseCamera(deviceId); if (!closed) { Console.WriteLine("Warning: Camera may not have closed properly"); } } }
Checks if a camera is currently open and connected to the hardware.
The unique device ID of the camera to check.
true if the camera is currently open and connected; false if the camera is closed, not found, or the device ID is invalid.
This method provides a quick way to check camera connection status without attempting to open or modify the camera state.
Thread Safety: This method is thread-safe and can be called from any thread.
Performance: This is a lightweight operation that only checks internal state.
string deviceId = "MyCamera_12345";
if (GenICamCameraManager.IsCameraOpen(deviceId)) { Console.WriteLine("Camera is ready for use"); var camera = GenICamCameraManager.GetCamera(deviceId); // Use camera... } else { Console.WriteLine("Camera needs to be opened first"); GenICamCameraManager.OpenCamera(deviceId); }
Forces removal and disposal of all cameras from the cache, regardless of their current state.
⚠️ WARNING: This method should be used with extreme caution as it will dispose all camera instances even if they are currently in use. This can cause exceptions in other parts of the application that are actively using cameras.
This method is intended for use in the following scenarios:
Application shutdown
Recovery from unrecoverable camera states
Memory cleanup in testing scenarios
Thread Safety: This method is thread-safe but will affect all threads using cameras.
Recovery: After calling this method, you must call to repopulate the camera cache before using cameras again.
// Application shutdown sequence try { // Attempt graceful shutdown first foreach (var deviceId in GetDeviceIds()) { CloseCamera(deviceId); } } catch (Exception ex) { Console.WriteLine($"Graceful shutdown failed: {ex.Message}"); } finally { // Force cleanup as last resort GenICamCameraManager.ForceCleanup(); }

// Find all cameras from vendors containing "Basler" var baslerCameras = GenICamCameraManager.FindCamerasByVendor("Basler"); Console.WriteLine($"Found {baslerCameras.Count} Basler cameras");
foreach (var camera in baslerCameras) { Console.WriteLine($" - {camera.DeviceId}"); }

The model name or partial model name to search for.

Performance: This method may take some time as it needs to query device information for each available camera.
Cameras that cannot be queried are skipped with a warning logged.
// Find all cameras with model names containing "ace" var aceCameras = GenICamCameraManager.FindCamerasByModel("ace"); Console.WriteLine($"Found {aceCameras.Count} cameras with 'ace' in model name");

Finds a camera by its exact serial number using case-insensitive matching.
The serial number to search for.
A instance with the matching serial number, or null if no camera with that serial number is found.
This method performs a case-insensitive exact match search for cameras with the specified serial number.
Performance: This method may take some time as it needs to query device information for each available camera until a match is found.
Cameras that cannot be queried are skipped with a warning logged.
Uniqueness: Serial numbers should be unique, so this method returns the first match found.
// Find camera by serial number var camera = GenICamCameraManager.FindCameraBySerialNumber("12345678"); if (camera != null) { Console.WriteLine($"Found camera: {camera.DeviceId}");
// Open and use the camera if (GenICamCameraManager.OpenCamera(camera.DeviceId)) { // Use camera... GenICamCameraManager.CloseCamera(camera.DeviceId); } } else { Console.WriteLine("Camera with serial number 12345678 not found"); }
Gets all cameras with their detailed information loaded by temporarily opening each camera.
A list of instances with their properties populated with detailed camera information.
This method temporarily opens each camera to read its detailed information, then closes it immediately. This provides comprehensive camera information but has the following implications:
Performance: This operation can be slow as it connects to each camera
Exclusive Access: Cameras in use by other applications will be skipped
Resource Usage: Temporarily uses camera resources for each device
Use Cases:
Camera discovery and enumeration interfaces
Detailed camera capability reporting
Camera selection based on specifications
Cameras that cannot be opened or provide information are excluded from the results.
// Get all cameras with detailed information var camerasWithInfo = GenICamCameraManager.GetCamerasWithInfo();
Console.WriteLine($"Found {camerasWithInfo.Count} cameras with detailed info:"); foreach (var camera in camerasWithInfo) { var info = camera.CameraInfo; Console.WriteLine($" - {info.DeviceId}"); Console.WriteLine($" Vendor: {info.Vendor}"); Console.WriteLine($" Model: {info.Model}"); Console.WriteLine($" Serial: {info.SerialNumber}"); Console.WriteLine($" Resolution: {info.Width}x{info.Height}"); }

Static methods to convert between different sample formats.
Code is mainly based on information available on the original C source code pa_converters.c from Portable Audio I/O Library.
This class try to be as fast as possible without using unsafe code.
Dither isn't currently supported. Currently supported conversions are 'to' and 'from' conversions between the following value types:
Integer 8-bit (byte), Integer 16-bit (Int16), Integer 32-bit (Int32), Single precision 32-bit floating point (float).
Which are the most common PCM formats.
To use it, just call Convert. The compiler will automatically detect which method to call based on your data types. Couldn't be simplier.
int[] srcPcm16samples = new int[] { 1, 2, 3}; float[] destIeeeFloat32samples = new float[3];
SampleConverter.Convert(srcPcm16samples, destIeeeFloat32samples);
// destIeeeFloat32samples now contains the converted samples.

Gets or sets time in milliSeconds that the DSP will wait to continue amplification, after the maximum has been reached.
Gets or sets the amplification for a channel. Default value is 10000, which means that no amplification occours. A value of 20000 raises the amplification by 2.

Provides utility methods for array manipulation operations including concatenation, copying between different array types, and comparison.
This internal helper class offers optimized array operations that are used throughout the VisioForge.Core library. It includes platform-specific optimizations for Windows using native memory comparison functions.
Concatenates multiple arrays of the same type into a single array.
The type of elements in the arrays. A variable number of arrays to concatenate. A new array containing all elements from the input arrays in the order they were provided.
This method efficiently concatenates multiple arrays by pre-calculating the total size and copying each array only once.
Concatenates two arrays of the same type into a single array.
The type of elements in the arrays. The first array to concatenate. This array will be resized to contain both arrays. The second array to concatenate. The resized first array containing all elements from both input arrays. Thrown when either or is null.
This extension method modifies the first array by resizing it to accommodate both arrays' contents.
Copies data from a byte array to a short array using unmanaged memory operations.
The source byte array to copy from. The destination short array to copy to. Must be properly sized to receive the data.
This method uses unmanaged memory as an intermediate buffer to perform the type conversion. The destination array must be properly sized: dst.Length should equal src.Length / 2.
Copies data from a short array to a byte array using unmanaged memory operations.
The source short array to copy from. The destination byte array to copy to. Must be properly sized to receive the data.
This method uses unmanaged memory as an intermediate buffer to perform the type conversion. The destination array must be properly sized: dst.Length should equal src.Length * 2.
Compares two byte arrays for equality using a managed byte-by-byte comparison.
The first byte array to compare. The second byte array to compare. The number of bytes to compare from the beginning of each array. true if the specified number of bytes are equal in both arrays; otherwise, false.
This method provides a cross-platform compatible array comparison but is slower than the native Compare method. Use this method on non-Windows platforms or when native interop is not available. The comparison stops at the first non-matching byte for efficiency.
Provides functionality to compare byte arrays for equality and generate hash codes for byte arrays. This class implements for byte arrays, allowing byte arrays to be used as keys in hash-based collections such as Dictionary and HashSet.
This comparer performs element-by-element comparison of byte arrays and generates hash codes based on the sum of all bytes in the array. Note that the hash code algorithm is simple and may not provide optimal distribution for all use cases.
Determines whether two byte arrays are equal by comparing their elements.
The first byte array to compare. Can be null. The second byte array to compare. Can be null.
true if both arrays are null, or if both arrays have the same length and contain the same sequence of bytes; otherwise, false.
This method handles null arrays gracefully. Two null arrays are considered equal. If only one array is null, they are considered not equal.
Generates a hash code for the specified byte array.
The byte array for which to generate a hash code. Must not be null.
A hash code calculated as the sum of all bytes in the array. This provides a simple hash that is sufficient for many use cases.
Thrown when is null.
The hash code is calculated by summing all byte values in the array. While simple, this approach may result in hash collisions for arrays with the same sum but different byte arrangements. For performance-critical applications with large datasets, consider using a more sophisticated hash algorithm.
Provides extension methods and utilities for converting SkiaSharp types to Cairo graphics library types.
This helper class is used internally to bridge the gap between SkiaSharp (used for cross-platform graphics) and Cairo (used by GStreamer for text and graphics rendering). All methods are extension methods that provide seamless conversion capabilities.
Converts a SkiaSharp color to a Cairo color.
The SkiaSharp color to convert. This color contains RGBA values in the range 0-255. A Cairo.Color instance with normalized RGBA values in the range 0.0-1.0.
This method normalizes the 8-bit color channel values (0-255) from SkiaSharp to the floating-point values (0.0-1.0) expected by Cairo.

A generic circular buffer implementation that allows efficient insertion and removal of elements at both ends of the buffer. When the buffer reaches full capacity, adding new elements will automatically remove elements from the opposite end.
When writing to a full buffer:
PushBack() removes the element at Front() (this[0])
PushFront() removes the element at Back() (this[Size-1])
This implementation is inspired by the Boost circular_buffer library: http://www.boost.org/doc/libs/1_53_0/libs/circular_buffer/doc/circular_buffer.html
The type of elements stored in the circular buffer.

The maximum number of elements that the buffer can hold. Must be positive. Initial items to fill the buffer with. The length must not exceed the capacity. Tip: Use Skip(x).Take(y).ToArray() to build this parameter from any enumerable. Thrown when capacity is less than 1 or when items length exceeds capacity. Thrown when items is null.
Gets the maximum capacity of the circular buffer.
When the buffer reaches maximum capacity (IsFull = true), pushing new elements will automatically remove elements from the opposite end to maintain the capacity limit.
The maximum number of elements that can be stored in the buffer.

When the buffer is full, adding new elements will cause elements to be removed from the opposite end of the buffer to maintain the capacity constraint.
true if the buffer contains the maximum number of elements; otherwise, false.

true if the buffer contains no elements; otherwise, false.
Gets the current number of elements contained in the circular buffer.
The number of elements currently stored in the buffer.
Returns the element at the front of the buffer without removing it.
The element at the front of the buffer (equivalent to this[0]). Thrown when the buffer is empty.
Returns the element at the back of the buffer without removing it.
The element at the back of the buffer (equivalent to this[Size - 1]). Thrown when the buffer is empty.
Gets or sets the element at the specified index in the buffer.
The zero-based index of the element to get or set. The element at the specified index.
The index does not wrap around; valid indices are in the range [0, Size).
Thrown when index is negative, greater than or equal to Size, or when the buffer is empty.
Adds an element to the back of the circular buffer.
The element to add to the back of the buffer.
After this operation, Back() and this[Size-1] will return the newly added element. If the buffer is full, the element at the front (Front()/this[0]) will be removed to make room for the new element.
Adds an element to the front of the circular buffer.
The element to add to the front of the buffer.
After this operation, Front() and this[0] will return the newly added element. If the buffer is full, the element at the back (Back()/this[Size-1]) will be removed to make room for the new element.
Removes and discards the element at the back of the circular buffer.
This operation decreases the buffer size by 1.
Thrown when the buffer is empty.
Removes and discards the element at the front of the circular buffer.
This operation decreases the buffer size by 1.
Thrown when the buffer is empty.
Removes all elements from the circular buffer.
After this operation, Size will be 0 but Capacity remains unchanged. All elements in the internal buffer are set to their default values.
Copies all elements from the circular buffer to a new array.
A new array containing copies of the elements in the buffer, ordered from front to back.
The returned array preserves the logical order of elements (from front to back), regardless of their physical arrangement in the internal buffer.
Gets the contents of the buffer as two ArraySegment instances without copying the elements.
An IList containing two ArraySegment instances that represent the buffer contents.
This method provides a zero-copy view of the buffer contents, which is useful for performance-critical scenarios such as network operations (e.g., Send(IList<ArraySegment<byte>>)).
The segments preserve the logical order of elements from front to back. Either or both segments may be empty depending on the buffer state.
Returns an enumerator that iterates through the circular buffer.
An enumerator that can be used to iterate through the buffer from front to back.
The enumeration preserves the logical order of elements regardless of their physical arrangement in the internal buffer.
Returns a non-generic enumerator that iterates through the circular buffer.
An IEnumerator that can be used to iterate through the buffer.
Throws an InvalidOperationException if the buffer is empty.
The error message to include in the exception. Defaults to "Cannot access an empty buffer." Thrown when the buffer is empty.
Increments the specified index by one, wrapping around to 0 when it reaches capacity.
A reference to the index variable to increment.
Decrements the specified index by one, wrapping around to capacity-1 when it reaches 0.
A reference to the index variable to decrement.
Converts a logical index (0 to Size-1) to the corresponding physical index in the internal buffer.
The logical index to convert. The corresponding physical index in the internal buffer array.
Gets the first contiguous segment of the circular buffer.
An ArraySegment representing the first contiguous portion of the buffer contents.
The circular buffer may be split into two segments due to wrapping. This method returns the first segment, which starts at the logical front of the buffer.
Gets the second contiguous segment of the circular buffer.
An ArraySegment representing the second contiguous portion of the buffer contents.
The circular buffer may be split into two segments due to wrapping. This method returns the second segment, which contains any wrapped-around elements. May return an empty segment if all elements are contiguous in the first segment.

This partial class of handles licensing-related functionalities. It provides a method to set the license key for the Live Video Compositor SDK.
Proper licensing is required to unlock the full features of the Live Video Compositor SDK. The license key, along with user details, is used to validate the software's usage.
// Example of setting the license key for the Live Video Compositor. // This should typically be done once at application startup. var compositor = new LiveVideoCompositor(); compositor.SetLicenseKey("YOUR_LICENSE_KEY", "Your Name", "your.email@example.com");
// After setting the license key, the SDK's features will be enabled according to the license level.
Advanced Live Video Compositor V2 providing next-generation real-time video composition and mixing capabilities. This version offers enhanced performance, improved GPU acceleration, advanced bridge architecture, and comprehensive multi-channel video/audio processing for professional live production workflows. Built on optimized GStreamer pipeline architecture with direct hardware acceleration support and advanced synchronization capabilities. Implements the . Implements the .
LiveVideoCompositor V2 enhancements include: - Improved GPU acceleration with optimized rendering pipelines - Advanced bridge architecture for better input/output isolation - Enhanced multi-channel processing with independent video channels - Better synchronization and timing control for professional workflows - Optimized memory management and resource utilization - Support for higher resolution and frame rate compositions - Advanced overlay and effects management with hardware acceleration - Professional-grade audio mixing with multi-channel support Designed for demanding live production environments requiring maximum performance and reliability.
// Creating a high-performance 4K live compositor var settings = new LiveVideoCompositorSettings(3840, 2160, new VideoFrameRate(60, 1)) { MixerType = LVCMixerType.OpenGL, VideoChannelCount = 4, MaxVideoInputsCount = 8, MaxVideoOutputsCount = 4 };
var compositor = new LiveVideoCompositor(context, settings); await compositor.StartAsync();
Partial class implementation of Live Video Compositor containing overlay management functionality. This part of the class handles the creation and management of video overlays that can be added to the composited video output.
This partial class extends the LiveVideoCompositor with overlay capabilities, allowing text, images, and other visual elements to be overlaid on the video stream. The overlay functionality is only available on non-Android platforms.
Provides video effects management functionality for the . This partial class allows adding, removing, and managing video effects on the compositor's output.
This partial class is part of the LiveVideoCompositor and specifically handles video effect operations. Effects are applied to the entire compositor output before it is sent to the various outputs. The effects system supports dynamic addition and removal of effects during playback.

UniformToFill scaling ensures that the entire target area is filled while maintaining the source aspect ratio. This may result in cropping parts of the source image. Defines the resize policy options for video inputs in the Live Video Compositor.
This enumeration controls how video inputs are scaled and positioned within their designated rectangle in the compositor. Each policy offers different trade-offs between preserving aspect ratio and filling the available space.
Scales the video to fit within the target rectangle while maintaining the original aspect ratio. Black bars (letterboxing or pillarboxing) are added as needed to fill the remaining space.
This mode ensures the entire source video is visible without any cropping. If the aspect ratios of source and target don't match, black bars will appear either on the sides (pillarboxing) or top/bottom (letterboxing) of the video.
Stretches the video to completely fill the target rectangle, ignoring the original aspect ratio.
This mode may cause visual distortion if the source and target aspect ratios differ significantly. Use this mode when you need to fill the exact rectangle dimensions and aspect ratio preservation is not important.
Scales the video to fill the entire target rectangle while maintaining the original aspect ratio. Parts of the video may be cropped to achieve this.
This mode ensures no black bars appear, but may crop portions of the source video to maintain the aspect ratio. The video is centered in the target rectangle, with equal amounts cropped from opposite sides when necessary. Also known as "zoom to fill" or "crop to fit".

Represents a video-only input source for the Live Video Compositor.
This class handles video input streams that will be composited into the final output. It supports various features including custom positioning, resize policies, optional preview rendering, and processing blocks for applying effects or transformations to the input video stream. Video inputs can be dynamically added, removed, and repositioned during playback.
The tee block (optional).
The video renderer.

The letterbox resize block.
Gets the video frame information for this input.
The video frame information containing width, height, format, and frame rate. This information is required and must be provided during construction.
Gets the list of video processing blocks applied to this input.
A list of instances that process the video stream. Processing blocks should not change the video dimensions - use a separate resize block if size changes are needed.
Processing blocks are applied in the order they appear in the list, after the source block but before the video is sent to the compositor mixer. Common uses include color correction, deinterlacing, or other video filters.
The rectangle.
Gets or sets the position and size of this video input within the compositor output.
A defining the position (x, y) and size (width, height) in pixels.
Changes to this property after playback has started will not take effect automatically. To update the rectangle during playback, use the compositor's Input_VideoStream_Update method. When ResizePolicy is set to LetterboxToFill, changing this property will automatically recalculate the crop area.
Gets or sets the z-order (layer position) of this video input.
The z-order value. Higher values appear on top of lower values. Default is 0.
Z-order determines the stacking order when multiple video inputs overlap. Inputs with higher z-order values will be rendered on top of those with lower values.
Gets or sets the resize policy for this video input.
The that determines how the video is scaled to fit its rectangle. Default is .
The resize policy controls how the input video is fitted into its designated rectangle, affecting whether aspect ratio is preserved and how empty space or overflow is handled.
Gets or sets an optional video view for previewing this input.
An instance for rendering a preview of this input, or null if no preview is needed.
When set, the input video will be duplicated and rendered to this view in addition to being sent to the compositor. This is useful for monitoring individual inputs. The preview uses a tee element to split the video stream without affecting the main composition.

Resource disposal and cleanup functionality for the Live Video Compositor. This partial class implements proper disposal patterns for releasing unmanaged resources, cleaning up MediaBlocks pipelines, and ensuring proper shutdown of composition operations. Provides both synchronous and asynchronous disposal methods for different cleanup scenarios. Implements the .
Disposal operations include: - Proper shutdown of MediaBlocks pipelines - Cleanup of video and audio mixers - Disposal of overlay managers and effects processors - Release of all input and output resources - Cleanup of tee blocks and bridge connections Both synchronous and asynchronous disposal patterns are supported for different use cases.
License management functionality for the Live Video Compositor. This partial class handles software license validation and activation for the Live Video Compositor component. License validation ensures compliance with VisioForge licensing terms and enables full functionality. Implements the .
License management includes: - License key validation and storage - User credential association (username, email) - Runtime license verification - Compliance with VisioForge licensing requirements Valid license is required for full Live Video Compositor functionality in production environments.
Provides real-time live video composition and mixing capabilities for multiple video and audio inputs. This class creates a complex MediaBlocks pipeline that can mix multiple video sources in real-time, apply video effects, manage overlay graphics, and route the composed output to multiple destinations. Supports CPU-based mixing, GPU-accelerated OpenGL mixing, Direct3D 11 composition (Windows), and input switching modes. Essential for live streaming, video production, broadcast applications, and multi-camera setups. Implements the . Implements the .
The Live Video Compositor manages multiple pipelines: - Main pipeline: Handles video/audio mixing and effects processing - Input pipelines: Each input source runs in its own pipeline for isolation - Output pipelines: Multiple outputs can be configured for different destinations The compositor uses bridge blocks to connect these separate pipelines efficiently.
// Create compositor with specific settings var settings = new LiveVideoCompositorSettings { VideoWidth = 1920, VideoHeight = 1080, VideoFrameRate = new VideoFrameRate(30, 1), MixerType = LVCMixerType.OpenGL, MaxVideoInputsCount = 4, MaxVideoOutputsCount = 2 };
using var compositor = new LiveVideoCompositor(settings);
// Add video inputs var input1 = new LVCVideoAudioInput("Camera 1", captureSettings); await compositor.Input_AddAsync(input1);
// Add output var output = new LVCVideoAudioOutput("RTMP Stream", rtmpSettings); await compositor.Output_AddAsync(output);
// Start composition await compositor.StartAsync();
Overlay management functionality for the Live Video Compositor. This partial class provides methods for adding, removing, updating, and managing video overlays on individual video channels within the composition pipeline. Overlays include text, images, graphics, and other visual elements that are composited on top of the video content in real-time.
Video overlay capabilities include: - Real-time overlay rendering during live composition - Per-channel overlay management for independent video processing - Dynamic addition, removal, and updates of overlays without stopping composition - Support for multiple overlay types (text, images, graphics, animations) - Z-order management for layered overlay composition - Hardware-accelerated overlay rendering when available Overlays are rendered in the order they are added to each channel, with later overlays appearing on top.
Video effects management functionality for the Live Video Compositor. This partial class provides methods for adding, updating, removing, and managing video effects on individual video channels within the composition pipeline. Effects are applied per-channel and can be dynamically added or removed during live composition operations. Implements the . Implements the . Implements the .
Video effects capabilities include: - Real-time effect application during live composition - Per-channel effect management for independent video processing - Dynamic addition and removal of effects without stopping composition - Effect parameter updates during live operation - Automatic pipeline state management during effect changes Effects are processed in the order they are added to each channel.

This method follows the standard IDisposable pattern. When disposing is true, both managed and unmanaged resources are released. When disposing is false (called from finalizer), only unmanaged resources are released.
Core disposal logic that releases all compositor resources.
This method is called by both synchronous and asynchronous disposal paths. It ensures all MediaBlocks components are properly disposed in the correct order: 1. Video and audio mixers 2. Tee blocks for splitting signals 3. Overlay managers (if not on Android) 4. All input sources 5. All output sinks
Finalizes an instance of the class.
The finalizer ensures that unmanaged resources are released even if Dispose was not called. This is a safety mechanism and should not be relied upon for proper cleanup. Always call Dispose() or use a using statement for deterministic cleanup.
Performs application-defined tasks associated with freeing, releasing, or resetting unmanaged resources.
This method should be called when the Live Video Compositor is no longer needed. It releases all resources including MediaBlocks pipelines, mixers, effects, and overlays. After disposal, the object cannot be used and should be discarded.
Asynchronously disposes of the Live Video Compositor and all its resources.
A ValueTask representing the asynchronous disposal operation.
This method provides asynchronous disposal support for scenarios where pipeline shutdown may involve asynchronous operations. It ensures proper cleanup of all MediaBlocks components without blocking the calling thread. Prefer this method over synchronous Dispose() when possible.

Configuration settings for the Live Video Compositor, defining video/audio format parameters, mixer technology, resource limits, and processing capabilities for real-time composition. These settings determine the compositor's output quality, performance characteristics, and capacity for handling multiple inputs and outputs.
The settings are immutable for video dimensions and frame rate once created, as these fundamental parameters affect the entire composition pipeline. Other settings like mixer type and capacity limits can be adjusted based on the target platform and performance requirements. Default values are optimized for common live streaming scenarios with balanced quality and performance.
// Create settings for 1080p live composition var settings = new LiveVideoCompositorSettings(1920, 1080, new VideoFrameRate(30, 1)) { MixerType = LVCMixerType.OpenGL, VideoChannelCount = 2, // Two independent video processing channels MaxVideoInputsCount = 6, MaxVideoOutputsCount = 3, AudioSampleRate = 48000, AudioChannels = 2 };
Gets or sets the type of the video mixer technology used for compositing multiple video streams.
The type of the video mixer. Default is D3D11 on Windows, OpenGL on other platforms.
Different mixer types offer varying performance characteristics: - D3D11: Best performance on Windows with DirectX 11 support - OpenGL: Cross-platform compatibility with good performance - Software: CPU-based mixing, most compatible but slowest
Gets the width of the video composition in pixels.
The width of the video composition. This value is immutable after creation.
Common values include 1920 (Full HD), 1280 (HD), 3840 (4K UHD). All inputs will be scaled/positioned within this resolution.
Gets the height of the video composition in pixels.
The height of the video composition. This value is immutable after creation.
Common values include 1080 (Full HD), 720 (HD), 2160 (4K UHD). All inputs will be scaled/positioned within this resolution.
Gets the video frame rate for the composition.
The video frame rate as a rational number (e.g., 30/1 for 30fps). This value is immutable after creation.
Common frame rates include 24, 25, 29.97, 30, 50, 59.94, and 60 fps. All inputs will be resampled to match this frame rate if different.
Gets or sets the number of independent video processing channels in the compositor.
The video channel count. Default is 1. Valid range is 1-16.
Multiple channels allow for independent video processing pipelines within the same compositor, useful for multi-view outputs or separate processing chains. Each channel can have its own set of inputs, effects, and outputs.
Gets or sets the audio sample format for the composition.
The audio format. Default is S16LE (16-bit signed little-endian).
Supported formats include: - S16LE: 16-bit signed PCM, most compatible - S32LE: 32-bit signed PCM, higher quality - F32LE: 32-bit float, professional quality
Gets or sets the audio sample rate in Hz for the composition.
The audio sample rate in Hz. Default is 48000 (48 kHz).
Common sample rates include: - 44100: CD quality - 48000: Professional audio/video standard - 96000: High-resolution audio All audio inputs will be resampled to match this rate if different.
Gets or sets the number of audio channels for the composition.
The number of audio channels. Default is 2 (stereo).
Common configurations: - 1: Mono - 2: Stereo (L/R) - 6: 5.1 surround - 8: 7.1 surround Audio inputs will be upmixed/downmixed to match this configuration.
Gets or sets the maximum number of video input sources that can be connected to the compositor.
The maximum video inputs count. Default is 4.
This value should be set based on expected usage and available system resources. Higher values allow more simultaneous video sources but require more memory and processing power. Typical use cases: 2-4 for basic mixing, 8-16 for complex productions.
Gets or sets the maximum number of video output destinations that can receive the composed video.
The maximum video outputs count. Default is 4.
Multiple outputs allow simultaneous streaming, recording, and preview. Common configurations: 1 for simple recording, 2-3 for streaming + recording, 4+ for multi-destination broadcasting.
Gets or sets the maximum number of audio input sources that can be connected to the compositor.
The maximum audio inputs count. Default is 4.
Audio inputs can include microphones, system audio, file sources, or network streams. Each input can be independently mixed with volume, panning, and effects control.
Gets or sets the maximum number of audio output destinations that can receive the mixed audio.
The maximum audio outputs count. Default is 4.
Multiple audio outputs enable scenarios like separate mix-minus feeds, multi-language outputs, or different audio processing chains.
Gets the unique random key assigned to this compositor instance.
The random key used for internal identification and bridge connections.
This key is automatically generated at creation and ensures unique identification of bridge connections between the main compositor and its inputs/outputs.
Initializes a new instance of the class with specified video dimensions and frame rate.
The width of the video composition in pixels. Must be greater than 0. The height of the video composition in pixels. Must be greater than 0. The frame rate of the composition as a rational number (e.g., new VideoFrameRate(30, 1) for 30fps).
The video dimensions and frame rate are immutable once set. The mixer type is automatically selected based on the platform: D3D11 for Windows, OpenGL for other platforms.
Live Video Compositor audio input that feeds audio content into the composition pipeline. Handles audio-only sources with format conversion, mixing, and processing capabilities within the audio composition. Each audio input maintains its own audio format specification and optional processing chain for effects or transformations. Implements the .
Audio inputs support: - Configurable audio format (sample rate, channels, bit depth) - Optional processing blocks for audio effects, normalization, or filtering - Dynamic audio info updates during playback via UpdateInfo method - Independent lifecycle management from the main compositor - Automatic format conversion to match compositor settings
// Creating an audio input with custom format var audioInfo = new AudioInfoX(AudioFormatX.S16LE, 48000, 2); var audioInput = new LVCAudioInput("Microphone", compositor, sourceBlock, audioInfo, autostart: true); await compositor.Input_AddAsync(audioInput);

Live Video Compositor audio output that receives composed audio content from the main composition pipeline. Handles audio-only destinations including file encoders, streaming outputs, audio monitoring, and hardware outputs. Each audio output maintains its own processing pipeline with format conversion to match the target destination requirements. Implements the .
Audio output types include: - File encoders (MP3, WAV, AAC) for recording composed audio - Streaming encoders (AAC for RTMP, Opus for WebRTC) for live broadcasting - Audio monitoring outputs for real-time audio monitoring - Hardware outputs (audio interfaces, headphones) for live monitoring - Network outputs (RTP audio) for distribution Automatic format conversion ensures compatibility with compositor settings and target destinations.
// Creating an audio output for file recording var audioOutput = new LVCAudioOutput("Audio Recording", compositor, audioEncoderBlock, autostart: true); await compositor.Output_AddAsync(audioOutput);
Initializes a new instance of the class.
The unique name identifying this audio output. The compositor instance that will provide audio to this output. The main media block that receives and processes the composed audio. if set to true, automatically starts with the main pipeline.
Live Video Compositor file-based video and audio input specifically optimized for media file playback within compositions. Handles video and audio content from file sources with specialized buffering and synchronization for non-live content. Uses BridgeBufferSinkBlock for video to provide optimal file-based media integration with the live composition pipeline. Implements the .
File-based inputs provide: - Optimized buffering for file sources via BridgeBufferSinkBlock - Synchronized video and audio playback from media files - Support for seeking, looping, and playback control - Independent processing blocks for video and audio effects - Custom synchronization flags for file-to-live timing alignment - Automatic format detection and conversion from file sources Designed specifically for integrating pre-recorded media into live compositions.
// Creating a file input for background video var fileInput = new LVCFileVideoAudioInput("Background", compositor, fileSourceBlock, videoInfo, audioInfo, new Rect(0, 0, 1920, 1080), autostart: true); await compositor.Input_AddAsync(fileInput);

Base class for Live Video Compositor input sources that feed media content into the composition pipeline. Each input runs in its own isolated MediaBlocks pipeline and connects to the main compositor via bridge blocks. This architecture allows for independent control of each input source (start, stop, pause) while maintaining synchronized output from the main composition pipeline. Supports video-only, audio-only, or combined video/audio inputs. Implements the .
Input types include: - Video capture devices (cameras, capture cards) - Audio capture devices (microphones, audio interfaces) - Network streams (RTSP, NDI, HTTP) - File-based sources (video files, image sequences) - Virtual sources (test patterns, screen capture) Each input maintains its own processing pipeline for isolation and independent lifecycle management.
// Creating a video input from a camera var cameraInput = new LVCVideoAudioInput("Camera 1", compositor, cameraSettings); cameraInput.Rectangle = new Rect(0, 0, 640, 480); // Position in composition await compositor.Input_AddAsync(cameraInput);
// The input will automatically start with the compositor await compositor.StartAsync();
